Propose the `## Design` rationale and the `design-significant:` marker for session 127.

Session 127 subject: **making a fleet handoff something a gate actually consumes.**

Context: The Vajra project has now built out its full SDLC agent fleet — nine roles (requirements-analyst, design-advisor, plan-advisor, implementation-advisor, demo-producer, qa-specialist, release-coordinator, fidelity-reviewer, researcher). Sessions 121–126 registered and scaffolded these roles. The open problem for S127 is that a "fleet handoff" (one role's output passed to the next role/stage) is currently just an advisory artifact — nothing in the pipeline's gates actually *consumes* it as a binding input. S127's job is to make a handoff a real, gate-consumed thing.

Your task (per your role — propose, do not implement):
1. Recommend whether S127 is design-significant (`design-significant: yes|no`) and justify it.
2. Draft the `## Design` rationale for the S127 prompt.
3. Cite a design record (ADR or decision) that ACTUALLY EXISTS under docs/adr/ or docs/decisions/ — verify it exists before citing; if the design deviates from it, name that. Do not invent an ADR id.

Read the repo as needed to ground your proposal (the existing gate/marker "house pattern" — existence-gated recorded markers — is central; see how Architect/Planner/Coder/QA stations gate on recorded markers). Return your brief.

1	# DECISION-007 — agent fleet, slice 1: a named role as a governed Claude Code subagent
2	
3	- **Date:** 2026-08-02 (Session 109)
4	- **Status:** ACCEPTED
5	- **Type:** architecture decision (a new product direction — the named-agent fleet)
6	- **Relates to:** DECISION-001 (governance is the product), DECISION-005 (autopilot trust — "leave a
7	  team of agents working, come back, trust the result"), and the S103 fleet-vs-gates fork (opened at
8	  the founder pivot; recommended shape = **both**). This decision resolves that fork for the FIRST
9	  slice only and locks the subagent dispatch + handoff mechanism it introduces.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Context — why decide now
14	
15	The product's headline is a **team** of agents you can trust unattended (DECISION-005). But in code,
16	`vajra claude` launches exactly **one** undifferentiated agent. The eight "stations" (S104) are
17	**gates + a team-voice roster** — labels over a single agent, not real separate agent invocations.
18	The fleet fork opened at S103 has **0 code**. B (installable v0.1) is complete (S106–S108), so A (the
19	fleet) is the right next leg — but a fleet is many sessions. This decision de-risks it by locking the
20	**one-agent-one-handoff primitive** before any parallelism or multi-stage orchestration is designed.
21	
22	## The fork, resolved (first slice only)
23	
24	**Both.** The fleet is **real named agents running behind the existing trust gates** — not a
25	gate-only pipeline, and not a fleet that routes around governance. This decision commits only to
26	slice 1 (**one** role, the Researcher); it does **not** design the whole fleet (parallelism, a second
27	role, multi-stage orchestration are all explicitly deferred).
28	
29	## Decision — the fleet is native Claude Code subagents, scaffolded + governed by Vajra
30	
31	A named role is a **native Claude Code subagent** (a `.claude/agents/<name>.md` definition the
32	running agent dispatches via its Task tool), NOT a fresh `claude -p` subprocess Vajra spawns.
33	
34	**Why the subagent model (chosen over a `claude -p` subprocess):** Vajra is an external binary — it
35	cannot *call* a Claude Code subagent (those exist only inside a running agent session). So Vajra's
36	role for a named agent is not "spawn the process" but **scaffold the role + govern its handoff** —
37	which is exactly what Vajra already is (the coach, not the coder; DECISION-001) and exactly how it
38	already scaffolds `.claude/settings.json` + hooks (S44). Concretely the subagent model:
39	
40	- **inherits the live session's auth** — no separate headless login. (S109 proved the alternative's
41	  cost: a `claude -p` subprocess hit a "Not logged in" headless-auth wall that only the human can
42	  clear. The subagent path has no such wall.)
43	- **is the native Claude Code idiom** — `.claude/agents/*.md` is the built-in "named role with a
44	  scoped prompt" mechanism; it maps 1:1 to this decision.
45	- **meters for free** — a subagent's cost rolls into the parent session's receipt (`meter`'s
46	  `subagent_dir` already accounts for it).
47	
48	Vajra's two jobs, both locked here:
49	
50	### 1. Scaffold the role as a subagent — one canonical source, rides `vajra init`
51	
52	`vajra init` writes `.claude/agents/<name>.md` for every role in `fleet::ROLES`, rendered by
53	`fleet::render_subagent_definition` (YAML frontmatter `name`/`description`/read-only `tools` + the
54	role's system prompt + a pointer to the governed handoff). The role text lives in **exactly one
55	place** (`fleet::ROLES` — the S104/S99 no-drift rule); the subagent file is a *rendering* of it, the
56	same way `.claude/settings.json` is scaffolded. The role source is **vendor-neutral**; only the
57	rendering is Claude-specific (v1 is Claude-first — ADR-0001 — so this matches the existing posture).
58	
59	### 2. Govern the handoff — rides `vajra next`, fail-closed
60	
61	The subagent returns a findings brief. `vajra next --role <name> --from <findings>` (or `--from -`
62	for stdin) wraps it into a **governed handoff**:
63	
64	- **Where:** `.ai/handoffs/session-{NN}-{role}.md` — the `.ai/` spine **is** the memory
65	  (`feedback-map-concepts-to-vajra`); no new store, no 8th artifact type, no 8th command.
66	- **What:** frontmatter (`role`, `session`, `agent`, `source-sha` = sha256 of the exact findings,
67	  `captured` timestamp, `cost_usd` = `null` for slice 1 — the subagent cost is in the session
68	  receipt, disclosed in the summary) + the findings body + a **`## Handoff Delta`** section.
69	- **Delta tracking:** `## Handoff Delta` records what this handoff adds vs the prior stage (slice 1
70	  has no prior handoff — the prior stage is the session prompt / Analyst's WHAT — so it records
71	  "new" + byte count; a re-run records the size change against the existing handoff).
72	- **Fail-closed:** an unknown role, a missing/empty findings file, or a handoff that would not
73	  validate all exit non-zero — an unusable handoff never reads as a successful step. The subagent is
74	  told NOT to author the frontmatter; Vajra owns the hash, timestamp, and delta.
75	
76	## Alternatives considered
77	
78	- **A `claude -p` subprocess Vajra spawns** (`vajra claude --role`, agent injectable via
79	  `VAJRA_AGENT_CMD`) — built first this session, then **replaced** (founder call): it needs headless
80	  credentials Vajra cannot supply (the S109 auth wall), and it makes Vajra a process-spawner rather
81	  than a coach. It could return later as an *unattended, no-parent-session* mode, but it is **not
82	  built** and is out of scope here.
83	- **A new `vajra research` / `vajra agent` top-level command** — rejected: breaks the max-7 rule for
84	  a capability existing commands already carry (`init` scaffolds, `next` governs).
85	- **A new handoff store (DB / `.vajra/` dir / JSON index)** — rejected: `.ai/` already IS the memory.
86	- **Designing the whole fleet now** — rejected as scope creep (the named key risk of S109).
87	
88	## Consequences
89	
90	- **Locked:** fleet = native Claude Code subagents behind the existing gates; `vajra init` scaffolds
91	  `.claude/agents/<name>.md` from the canonical `fleet::ROLES`; `vajra next --role <name> --from`
92	  governs the findings into `.ai/handoffs/session-{NN}-{role}.md` with the frontmatter + `## Handoff
93	  Delta` contract; unknown role / missing-or-empty findings / malformed handoff all fail closed.
94	- **Deferred (need their own decision):** a second/third role, parallel dispatch, multi-stage
95	  orchestration, per-subagent cost in the handoff, an unattended `claude -p` dispatch mode.
96	- **Reversible?** Additive — nothing existing changes behavior. A later decision can extend the
97	  handoff contract or add the unattended dispatch mode without breaking slice-1 artifacts.
98	
99	## S111 addendum — the def-vs-dispatch wire, closed with on-disk proof
100	
101	S109 proved the scaffold and a real subagent run **separately**: the live run was dispatched by
102	handing the Task tool a hand-typed copy of the canonical prompt, not by resolving `subagent_type`
103	against the scaffolded file. S111 closed this:
104	
105	- **The mechanism (confirmed, not assumed):** Claude Code auto-discovers project-level
106	  `.claude/agents/<name>.md` files into available subagent types **once, at session start**. A file
107	  written mid-conversation is invisible to that same conversation (verified as a real negative
108	  result — see `sessions/session-111-artifacts/researcher-run-note.md`). A **fresh** session
109	  (`vajra claude` in a freshly-`vajra init`'d repo) that is asked to "use the researcher subagent"
110	  dispatches it **by that name** — confirmed by TWO independently-written Claude Code files agreeing
111	  on a random tool-call ID they didn't choose, not by a single copy-pasted JSON blob: the parent
112	  session's transcript records `subagent_type: "researcher"` on tool call `toolu_01BUEt…`
113	  (`researcher-parent-tooluse.json`), and the subagent's own `agent-<id>.meta.json` independently
114	  records `toolUseId: toolu_01BUEt…` resolved to `agentType: "researcher"` — same ID, two files,
115	  two different Claude Code runtime paths. The raw subagent transcript is captured byte-for-byte too
116	  (`researcher-subagent-transcript.jsonl`, sha256 cited in the run note). Full evidence:
117	  `sessions/session-111-artifacts/`.
118	- **Cost, checked not guessed, and re-runnable:** `scripts/check-subagent-cost-fields.sh` scans
119	  every real subagent JSONL transcript on the checking machine (not a one-off count baked into a
120	  doc-comment) for `total_cost_usd` / `cost_usd`. Zero found, at every run so far including S111's
121	  own dispatch. A subagent never produces the headless `-p` result stream that field lives on
122	  (S77/S78 root cause), so the figure structurally does not exist for Vajra to read. `cost_usd: null`
123	  stays, now for a specific, falsifiable, checked, **re-runnable** reason — anyone can re-run the
124	  script and get the same answer, and `--assert-null` turns it into a regression check.
125	- **Consequence:** the fleet's first slice is fully wired end-to-end — scaffold (`vajra init`) →
126	  live dispatch-by-name (Claude Code's own mechanism, a fresh session) → governed handoff
127	  (`vajra next --role --from`). No code change was needed to the dispatch path itself; S109 had
128	  already built it correctly. What was missing was the proof, which S111 supplies.
129	
130	## S113 addendum — the SECOND role is the **Reviewer** (chosen, not built)
131	
132	**Status: CHOSEN.** S113's deliverable was to pick the second role from evidence and record why;
133	building it is its own session (the S109 anti-scope-creep rule still applies). No `fleet::ROLES`
134	entry, no `.claude/agents/reviewer.md`, no code ships with this addendum.
135	
136	### The evidence that drove it (all from this repo, countable)
137	
138	1. **It is the one dispatch this repo already performs every single session — 46 times.**
139	   `ls sessions/*-review.md` = **46** independent cold reviews, S55 through S112, plus S67/S112/S113
140	   running it TWICE. It is not a hypothetical role; it is the fleet's busiest real job, running
141	   today with no scaffold at all.
142	2. **The constitution mandates it and forbids the alternative.** DECISION-002 + the "No
143	   self-certification" hard rule: fidelity must be judged by an independent pass fed only the prompt
144	   and the diff. Every session is contractually obliged to dispatch this agent.
145	3. **Today its prompt is HAND-TYPED each session — the exact drift the `fleet::ROLES` single source
146	   exists to kill.** The Researcher's instructions live in one canonical place and render into the
147	   subagent file; the Reviewer's do not live anywhere. Review quality therefore varies with how
148	   carefully the builder re-wrote the brief that day. Two sessions running (S112, S113) the
149	   carry-forward notes say "reuse the two-pass pattern" — a convention kept in prose, not in code.
150	4. **Its output already has a governed home and teeth.** `sessions/session-NN-review.md` is read by
151	   `verify-closeout.sh` (missing/hollow/REJECT all FAIL), attested by `Review-Inputs-SHA`
152	   (DECISION-003), chained in the ledger (DECISION-004), and counted by the Reviewer station. A
153	   Reviewer role is the shortest distance from "role scaffolded" to "role's output already gated" —
154	   every other candidate would need new machinery first.
155	5. **It needs read-only tools only** — the same posture as the Researcher (`Read, Grep, Glob`,
156	   plus git reads for the diff). No new trust surface: a fleet role that could WRITE would be a
157	   materially bigger decision, and this one avoids it.
158	
159	### Alternatives considered, and why each loses
160	
161	- **A Planner / Architect role (an agent that authors the `## Plan` or `## Design`).** Rejected:
162	  those stations "surface and enforce, never author" (S64, S67) — the human/parent agent owns the
163	  content and the gate checks it. A role that authors what a gate then grades is self-certification
164	  wearing a second hat.
165	- **A Coder role.** Rejected for now: it needs write tools, which is a genuinely larger governance
166	  decision (what may it edit, under whose approval token, against which commit gate), and the main
167	  agent already does this work under the existing gates.
168	- **A QA / verifier role.** Rejected: the QA station re-runs `verify-session-NN.sh` **live** (S69).
169	  A live green script is stronger evidence than an agent's opinion about the script — adding an
170	  agent here would swap teeth for prose.
171	- **A Demo-er / Releaser role.** Rejected: both are mechanical and derived from git and script
172	  output; there is no judgment for an agent to add.
173	
174	### Known limits of this choice (disclosed now, so the build session cannot claim more)
175	
176	- Scaffolding the Reviewer makes its brief **canonical and re-runnable**; it does **not** by itself
177	  make the review more independent than today's ad-hoc dispatch. Independence comes from the
178	  context boundary (a subagent gets a fresh context window, fed only the prompt + the diff), which
179	  already holds today.
180	- A scaffolded role is only as good as its dispatch: like the Researcher, a `.claude/agents/*.md`
181	  written mid-session is invisible to that same session (S111). The Reviewer role will land in one
182	  session and first be dispatchable by name in the next.
183	- **Name collision to resolve at build time (cold-review finding, S113):** the pipeline already has
184	  a **Reviewer station** (the eighth station in `K of 8`, `stations::reviewer_status`). A fleet role
185	  keyed `reviewer` would read ambiguously against it — "Reviewer PASSED" would mean the station,
186	  while "fleet: 1 governed handoff — reviewer" would mean the agent. The build session must either
187	  pick a distinct role key (e.g. `fidelity-reviewer`) or state explicitly that the role IS the
188	  station's agent. Do not leave it implicit.
189	
190	## S114 addendum — the Reviewer BUILT, and the two open items closed
191	
192	**Status: BUILT.** S113 chose the role; S114 ships it as a second `fleet::ROLES` entry rendered by
193	the same machinery (no second scaffolding path, no second handoff writer, no second role-text
194	source). The S113 addendum left two questions open and forbade leaving them implicit. Both are
195	decided here, and the code matches.
196	
197	### Open item 1 — the role key: **`fidelity-reviewer`** (a distinct key)
198	
199	The pipeline's eighth station is already called the **Reviewer** (`stations::reviewer_status`,
200	counted in `K of 8`). A role keyed `reviewer` would put the same word on two different things in
201	adjacent lines of the same report — `Reviewer PASSED` (the station) directly above `fleet: 1
202	governed handoff — reviewer` (the agent).
203	
204	**Decision: the role key is `fidelity-reviewer`.** Rejected the alternative ("state that the role IS
205	the station's agent") because it is not true: the station passes on an *attested review artifact
206	existing and not saying REJECT*, which a human can satisfy with no agent at all. The station measures
207	the artifact; the role produces one input to it. Two different things deserve two different names.
208	
209	Consequences, all mechanical: the subagent is `.claude/agents/fidelity-reviewer.md`, the handoff is
210	`.ai/handoffs/session-NN-fidelity-reviewer.md`, the dispatch is `subagent_type:
211	"fidelity-reviewer"`, and `vajra next --role reviewer` FAILS with the known-roles list (asserted by
212	test — `resolve_role("reviewer").is_none()`).
213	
214	### Open item 2 — the handoff vs `sessions/session-NN-review.md`: **pre-stage input, one record of record**
215	
216	The fidelity verdict already has a governed home with teeth: `sessions/session-NN-review.md` is read
217	by `verify-closeout.sh` (missing / hollow / REJECT all FAIL), attested by `Review-Inputs-SHA`
218	(DECISION-003), and chained in the ledger (DECISION-004). The failure mode to avoid is two competing
219	records of the same judgment.
220	
221	**Decision: the governed handoff is a PRE-STAGE INPUT — the captured raw verdict, hashed and
222	timestamped at the moment the agent returned it. `sessions/session-NN-review.md` remains the single
223	RECORD OF RECORD and the only thing any gate reads.** Rejected "pointer only" (a pointer throws away
224	the `source-sha` — the whole reason a handoff is evidence rather than prose) and rejected "the
225	handoff replaces the review artifact" (it would strip the attestation + ledger chain that make the
226	verdict tamper-evident, trading teeth for a newer file).
227	
228	How the code matches, not just the prose:
229	- The role's system prompt — the ONE canonical source, rendered verbatim into the subagent file —
230	  ends by stating the verdict is a pre-stage input, that `sessions/session-NN-review.md` is the
231	  canonical gated record, and that this agent does not write it.
232	- The role has **no write tool** (`Read, Grep, Glob`), so it *cannot* author the record of record.
233	- Nothing in `verify-closeout.sh` or the Reviewer station learns to read the handoff. The gate keeps
234	  reading exactly one artifact. A session that never dispatches the role closes exactly as before.
235	
236	### What this addendum does NOT claim
237	
238	- Scaffolding the role does not make the review more independent than today's hand-typed dispatch —
239	  independence comes from the fresh context window, which already held (S113 addendum, restated).
240	- Like every role, a `.claude/agents/*.md` written mid-session is invisible to that same session's
241	  Task tool (S111). The Reviewer role lands at S114 and is first dispatchable **by name** at S115.
242	- `fleet: 2 governed handoff(s)` certifies **two contract-valid files exist**, never that two agents
243	  ran (the standing S113 reading rule).
244	- A third role remains a separate decision. Two roles is not a fleet; it is two roles.
245	
246	### Open item 3 — found by THIS session's cold review: `reviewer/SKILL.md` was already a second source

336	### The role key: **`qa-specialist`** (a distinct key)

338	Third instance of the same collision the S114 and S116 addenda each closed. The pipeline already has
339	a **QA station** (`src/qa/mod.rs`, S69), counted in `K of 8`. A role keyed `qa` would put the same

342	handoff — qa` (the agent: a subagent that ran the suite and classified its checks).
343	
344	**Decision: the role key is `qa-specialist`.** `resolve_role("qa")` returns `None` and
345	`vajra next --role qa` fails with the known-roles list, asserted by test.
346	
347	**The station is not touched, and does not learn the role key.** The QA STATION governs the
348	process (did a recorded, executable marker actually re-run and pass?); the QA ROLE does the work
349	(run it, and say which of its checks were real). Same separation as Reviewer/`fidelity-reviewer`
350	and Planner/`plan-advisor`.

352	### The tool grant: **`Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob`** — the first executing role
353	
354	Every role before this one is read-only, and the S114 note in `Role::tools` said plainly that a
355	role which could write is "a materially bigger governance decision (DECISION-007) and none is taken
356	here." It is taken here, scoped to this one role.
357	
358	**Why Bash is load-bearing.** S118 and S120 measured the failure this role exists to catch: verify
359	suites can be built largely out of greps that find a message string in `src/` and call that proof
360	the feature works — checks that would still pass with the feature deleted. A read-only agent
361	auditing that problem can only grep for the greps. An agent that runs the suite either has an exit
362	code and real output, or it has nothing; it cannot physically fake a pass. Treating the root cause
363	means the QA agent must be an executor.
364	
365	**Considered and rejected:**
366	- **Rejected — a read-only QA agent (`Read, Grep, Glob`), like the other three.** It would produce
367	  exactly the artifact this session exists to stop trusting: prose about source it read, with no
368	  live evidence behind it. It could report that `verify-session-NN.sh` *contains* an execute-based
369	  check without ever learning whether that check passes, and its own findings would be the same
370	  class of hollow evidence it was hired to name. The role would be theatre.
371	- **Rejected — `Bash` only (no `Write`/`Edit`).** Considered as the minimal grant, and it is
372	  genuinely narrower. Rejected because the role's own contract requires it to hand back a findings
373	  brief that Vajra then governs via `vajra next --role qa-specialist --from <file>` — a file on
374	  disk — and because a real QA pass writes scratch: captured logs, a reduced repro, a temp fixture.
375	  Forcing all of that through stdout would push the agent toward `bash -c 'cat > file'`, which is
376	  the same capability with the audit trail removed. The narrowing that actually matters is stated
377	  in the role prompt instead: do not edit the product under test, do not repair the checks you
378	  criticise, do not commit.
379	- **Rejected — grant the existing `fidelity-reviewer` a Bash tool instead of adding a role.** It
380	  collapses two jobs that must stay independent: the Reviewer grades requirements from the prompt
381	  and the diff and must not be able to run (or fix) the thing it judges; the QA Specialist produces
382	  the evidence, and explicitly does not issue the verdict. Merging them would also silently widen

384

386	The prompt forbids touching the product under test, but the tools do not enforce that — this is a
387	prompt-level constraint, not a sandbox. It is disclosed here rather than hidden behind "the role
388	is told not to." The existing L2/L3 hooks (`hook-pre-write.sh`, `hook-commit-guard.sh`,
389	`VAJRA_ALLOW_COMMIT`) still apply to anything the agent does inside a governed repo, so the
390	commit path in particular stays closed by machinery, not by instruction.

393	
394	- Same standing limit as the S113/S114/S116 addenda: a `.claude/agents/*.md` written mid-session is
395	  invisible to that same session's Task tool (S111). The role lands at S121 and is first
396	  dispatchable **by name** at S122 or later. **This session does not dispatch it.**
397	- `fleet: N governed handoff(s)` certifies **N contract-valid files exist**, never that N agents
398	  ran (the standing S113 reading rule).
399	- The role does not gain a new parser, a new artifact type, or an 8th command; it rides `init` and
400	  `next` exactly as roles 1–3 do, and it is reported BESIDE `K of 8`, never inside it (S113).
401	- Granting execution to this role grants it to no other. The allowlist is one name, asserted by a
402	  test that fails if a fifth role inherits Bash by being added to the table.
403	- A fifth role remains a separate decision.

405	## S122 addendum — the executor thesis is UNPROVEN (correction, not a new decision)
406	
407	The S121 addendum above argues the QA role must be an executor because an executor "cannot
408	physically fake a pass". **That claim is unproven and must not be repeated as measured.** This
409	addendum corrects the record; the decision itself (the role, the key, the `Bash, Read, Write, Edit,
410	Grep, Glob` grant) is unchanged.
411	
412	- **What two live runs actually measured.** The role has now run twice — the S121 post-close audit
413	  of `verify-session-121.sh`, and the S122 audit of this session's own suites. Between them it
414	  found **seven real defects**. Every single one came from careful independent READING. Execution
415	  bought the exit codes and the pass counts; it produced no finding on either run.
416	- **What IS evidenced: INDEPENDENCE, not execution.** An agent that did not build the thing finds
417	  defects the builder cannot see. That is the load-bearing property, and it is the property the
418	  read-only Fidelity Reviewer already had. Execution is a convenience for gathering evidence, not
419	  the mechanism that catches the lie.
420	- **What is NOT evidenced.** Nothing has tested whether an executor can fake a pass. No check in
421	  this repo attempts it.
422	- **The residual risk named in the S121 addendum is unchanged and unfenced.** The `Write`/`Edit`
423	  grant is documented, not controlled. On both live runs the working tree was byte-identical
424	  before and after — verified, not trusted — but in the agent's own words, *"that constraint held
425	  because I chose to hold it, which is not a control."* Fencing it is the leading candidate for
426	  the next session.
427	- **Where this correction is repeated:** `src/fleet/mod.rs` module header and the QA role's doc
428	  comment, both S122 verify-suite headers, and `scripts/demo-session-122.sh`. Anywhere the QA role
429	  is described, the thesis is described as unproven.

431	## S123 addendum — fencing the `Write`/`Edit` grant (the last self-granted jurisdiction)
432	
433	The S121/S122 addenda both name the same open risk: `qa-specialist`'s `Write`/`Edit` grant is
434	documented, not controlled. This addendum records the fence — and, first, the measurement the
435	S122 `qa-specialist` report itself demanded: *"Nothing proves the runtime honours `tools:`."*
436	
437	### Measurement — is a role's `tools:` grant actually enforced, or only a convention?
438	
439	Tested live, in this session, against the real dispatch mechanism (not a mock): the `researcher`
440	role — already a real, session-boot-registered subagent, granted `Read, Grep, Glob, WebSearch,
441	WebFetch`, no `Write`/`Edit`/`Bash` — was dispatched with an explicit instruction to attempt
442	writing a file by any means it could find, and to report the raw mechanism, not to reason about
443	whether it should comply.
444	
445	**Full evidence, captured and cross-verified, is
446	`sessions/session-123-artifacts/tools-enforcement-measurement.md`** — not asserted here as prose.
447	It reuses the exact evidentiary shape the S111 addendum used to prove a real by-name dispatch: two
448	independently-written files (this session's own transcript, and the dispatched subagent's separate
449	`meta.json`) agreeing on the same random tool-call ID (`toolu_01BpAnw69h7MVcRAZjbjYQo1`) neither
450	side controlled, plus the subagent's tool call and final report quoted verbatim. **A cold
451	`fidelity-reviewer` pass rejected the first cut of this addendum for exactly the gap that artifact
452	closes** — the claim below was true but, as first written, unfalsifiable narrative with nothing to
453	check it against.
454	
455	**Result: the grant IS enforced, mechanically, at the tool-definition level — not a prompt-level
456	convention the agent chooses to follow.** The dispatched agent reported no `Write`, `Edit`, or
457	`Bash` function was present in its callable tool schema at all: "not disabled, not erroring, simply
458	absent from the list of callable functions I was given." There was no rejected call and no error
459	text to quote, because there was nothing to call. The target file was confirmed absent afterward.
460	
461	**What this measurement does and does not license.** It proves the harness will not hand a
462	role a tool outside its recorded grant. It does **not** prove that dropping `Write`/`Edit` from
463	`qa-specialist` would close the write path — `qa-specialist` keeps `Bash` (it must, to run the
464	verify script), and a granted `Bash` tool can write a file by shell redirection
465	(`echo x > src/foo.rs`) with no `Write`/`Edit` tool involved at all. The measurement licenses only
466	this: narrowing `Write`/`Edit` is not worth *zero* (it closes one real, now-confirmed-enforced
467	path), but it is not the fence — `Bash` is the fence-defeating grant, and it cannot be removed
468	without removing the role's entire reason to exist.
469	
470	### Decision — route the dispatch through the existing clean-room runner (`src/gate_run.rs`, S119)
471	
472	`qa-specialist`'s dispatch is pointed at a disposable `git worktree add --detach HEAD` checkout,
473	not the source repo, via two new flags riding the existing `--role` surface (no 8th top-level
474	command): `vajra next --role qa-specialist --clean-room-open` materialises the worktree and prints
475	its path (gated: a role without a `Bash` grant is refused — nothing to isolate); `--clean-room-close
476	<path>` removes it once the run is done. `gate_run::CleanRoom::open_persistent`/`remove_persistent`
477	reuse the exact worktree-add/-remove primitives `qa_gate`'s `CleanRoom` already uses for the S119
478	live re-run — split out of that struct's `new`/`Drop` so a **fleet role's** dispatch (which happens
479	in a separate, longer-lived Claude Code session, not inside a single `vajra` process) can hold the
480	same checkout open across process boundaries instead of it being removed the instant the CLI call
481	that created it returns.
482	
483	**Considered and rejected — narrow the grant alone (drop `Write`/`Edit`, keep `Bash`).** The
484	measurement above shows this is not worthless, but it is not sufficient: the role needs `Bash` to
485	run the suite, and anything that can run a shell command can write a file. A fence that closes the
486	tool path while leaving the command path wide open is exactly the fake-green shape S122 spent four
487	review passes removing — it would look like a fence and not be one. **Kept as a cheap SECOND
488	layer** alongside the clean room, not as the fence itself; not yet applied to the scaffolded grant
489	this session (recorded as the residual, not silently done).
490	
491	**Considered and rejected — a hook that blocks writes during a QA run.** The only option that
492	requires *guessing intent*: the guard would need to know a given write came from the dispatched
493	subagent specifically (unverified, and per the measurement above the harness gives no signal for
494	this), and to close the `Bash` path it would have to parse arbitrary shell to decide "is this
495	write-shaped" — unwinnable in general (`printf`, `dd`, `tee`, a Python one-liner, redirection
496	through a pipe of unknown depth). A fence made of *rules* has to be right about everything a
497	malicious or confused agent might try; a fence made of *walls* only has to exist.
498	
499	### Residual risk — stated plainly, not softened
500	
501	**The clean room isolates the REPO, not the MACHINE.** `qa-specialist` still holds `Bash`, and the
502	real repo still exists on disk at a known absolute path — nothing stops `cd /path/to/real/repo &&
503	echo x > src/foo.rs`. What the clean room does is remove every *legitimate reason* to touch the
504	original and make any touch to it **detectable**: the source repo's `HEAD` sha, `git ls-files -s`
505	hash, and `git status --porcelain` are compared before and after (`verify-session-123.sh`'s
506	falsifiability fixture, S123 step 5) — the same technique the S121/S122 live runs already used by
507	hand. The honest claim is **isolation by default plus tamper-evidence as the backstop** — the same
508	posture as the verdict ledger (`DECISION-004`), which is tamper-**evident**, not tamper-**proof**.
509	Do not write "the QA role cannot modify the repo." Write what is true: it is not pointed at the
510	repo, and if it reaches for it anyway, that is visible. Anything stronger needs OS-level
511	sandboxing (a filesystem namespace, a container, a restricted user) — a different session, and
512	probably a different product surface than a CLI that scaffolds `.claude/` files.
513	
514	**This does not touch the executor thesis.** The S122 addendum retracted the claim that an
515	executor "cannot physically fake a pass" — this session does not restore it. Fencing removes one
516	specific way `qa-specialist` could cheat (repair the product, then report the repaired state as the
517	original). It does not establish that no executor can fake a pass by any means, and the property
518	actually evidenced by both live runs remains INDEPENDENCE, not execution. Never restate the S121
519	claim as measured because this fence now exists.
